title: El regateo
goal: Haggle properly, which is neither arguing nor accepting
culture: Haggling has a shape: ask, be told, counter once, meet in the middle, close, and never reopen it. Grinding somebody down is not winning and paying the first number is not manners — the ritual is the point, and both of you are meant to enjoy it.

beats.es: Ese bolso de cuero le sale en mil quinientos. De Masaya, hecho a mano.
beats.en: Would you let me have it for a thousand?
beats.good: One counter, said as a question. Me lo deja en... is not an argument — it is the next line of a script you are both reading from.

beats.es: ¿Mil? Uy, no. En mil doscientos, y le juro que no gano nada.
beats.objective: Split it — say it suits neither of you
beats.key: ni para usted ni para mí
beats.say: Mil cien. Ni para usted ni para mí.
beats.en: Eleven hundred. Good for neither of us.
tiles: ni para usted ni para mí
ok: mil cien ni para usted ni para mi
ni para usted ni para mi
teaches: ni para usted ni para mí
beats.good: Ni para usted ni para mí closes the gap by making the split the fair thing rather than the concession. It lets him agree without losing.

beats.es: Ay, hombre. Mil ciento cincuenta y se lo llevo hasta la esquina.
beats.good: Ya pues is come on, alright, enough — a nudge and not a demand. Said with a smile it ends the haggling your way and costs him nothing he minds.

beats.es: ¡Bueno! Mil cien pues. Se lo dejo porque usted me cae bien.
beats.good: Trato hecho — done. Say it, pay it, and never go back to the price: reopening a closed deal is the one genuinely rude move in the whole exchange.
